title: Quantum Bloch group: framework connection and the pre-archimedean refinement
html:
The pentagon identity of the quantum dilogarithm \Phi_q — the Yang–Baxter equation in exponential form — connects to the QOU framework as follows:

  1. The braid group B_n is generated by the Yang–Baxter equation \sigma_i\sigma_{i+1}\sigma_i = \sigma_{i+1}\sigma_i\sigma_{i+1}.

  2. The Hecke relation \sigma_i^2 = h_{\mathrm{A}}\sigma_i + 1 is the linearisation of the quantum pentagon identity.

  3. The traced volumes \hat{V}_i(q) satisfy the Hecke relation because they are matrix elements of \rho(\sigma_i) in the standard representation.

  4. The algebraic quantum volume \mathrm{Vol}_q = \prod \hat{V}_i therefore satisfies the pentagon identity (multiplicatively), and its logarithm \Phi_1 = \tfrac{1}{2}\sum \ln(\hat{V}_i \cdot \overline{\hat{V}_i}) satisfies the five-term relation (additively).

This explains why \Phi_1 is a quantum dilogarithm: the traced volumes are exponentials of quantum dilogarithm values, and their product lives in the quantum Bloch group. The regulator map \mathfrak{B}(q) \to \mathbb{R} sends the algebraic volume to the hyperbolic volume, recovering \mathrm{Vol}(S^3 \setminus K) from the algebraic data. The classical counterpart of this sentence is proved for the A-polynomial curve Y of a knot rather than for \mathfrak{B}(q): the regulator 1-form \eta(l,m) = \log|l|\,d\arg m - \log|m|\,d\arg l is exact on the hyperbolic component, and its loop integrals, divided by 4\pi^2, lie in \tfrac{1}{N}\mathbb{Z}, where N is the order of the symbol \{l,m\} in K_2(\mathbb{C}(Y)) [li-wang2006, Thm. 3.3]. That theorem does not treat the quantum Bloch group, so the passage from \mathfrak{B}(q) to the regulator above is not covered by it.

Two published constructions sit beside this picture, each with a limit. On the classical side, the branch ambiguity of the dilogarithm is resolved by the extended Bloch group \widehat{\mathcal{B}}(\mathbb{C}) of flattened shape parameters: the extended Rogers dilogarithm gives a well-defined map R\colon\widehat{\mathcal{B}}(\mathbb{C})\to\mathbb{C}/\pi^2\mathbb{Z}, and its composite with H_3(\mathrm{PSL}(2,\mathbb{C});\mathbb{Z})\to\widehat{\mathcal{B}}(\mathbb{C}) computes volume and Chern--Simons invariant together, where the ordinary Bloch group fixes the Chern--Simons part only up to an additive ambiguity [neumann2004, §1]. On the q-side, for a number field F Garoufalidis, Scholze, Wheeler and Zagier construct a Habiro ring of F and a regulator K_3(F)\to\mathrm{Pic} of that ring, whose image line bundles carry q-series from perturbative Chern--Simons theory as sections; this geometry disappears after (q-1)-completion [wagner2025, §1.1]. Neither construction is the quantum Bloch group \mathfrak{B}(q) of this paper: the first is classical, and the second lives over the Habiro ring of a number field rather than over \widehat{\mathbb{Z}[q]} with the bar involution. They are recorded as the nearest literature statements of the same shape, not as cases of the claim above.

The Kashaev invariant is the state sum version: \langle K \rangle = \sum_j \prod_{\text{tetrahedra}} \Phi_q(x_j)^{\pm 1}, living in the Habiro ring. For the Borromean rings, this gives \langle \mathcal{B}_3 \rangle whose archimedean evaluation yields 8G.

Pre-archimedean side: \mathfrak{B}(\widehat{\mathbb{Z}[q]})

The quantum Bloch group \mathfrak{B}(q) has a natural pre-archimedean refinement over the Habiro ring \widehat{\mathbb{Z}[q]} (Habiro 2002), without passing through the complex numbers:

Side Bloch group Regulator \Phi_1 Where
Pre-archimedean \mathfrak{B}(\widehat{\mathbb{Z}[q]}) \tfrac{1}{2}\sum \ln(\hat{V}_i \cdot \overline{\hat{V}_i}) Habiro ring; bar = q \leftrightarrow q^{-1}
Archimedean (\tau_{\mathrm{arch}} at real q_0, real \hat{V}_i) \mathcal{B}(\mathbb{C}) \sum \ln\lvert\hat{V}_i\rvert Borel regulator r_1: K_1(\mathbb{C}) \to \mathbb{R}

The bar-involution form \tfrac{1}{2}\ln(V \cdot \overline{V}) at the pre-archimedean level is what the framework uses for \rho_K's single-generator piece ([prop:rho-k-graded-expansion](rho-k-graded-expansion.md)). At the archimedean specialization with real q_0 and real \hat{V}_i, this reduces to the classical Borel regulator \sum \ln\lvert\hat{V}_i\rvert — the form that appears in Borromean rings represent a non-trivial element of K_3(\mathbb{C}) / Bloch group with regulator r_2 = 8G under the Beilinson regulator r_2: K_3(\mathbb{C}) \to \mathbb{R}.

This makes the QOU framework's K-theoretic content categorically explicit: \rho_K is a graded regulator on \mathfrak{B}(\widehat{\mathbb{Z}[q]}) whose archimedean evaluation at q_0 \in \mathbb{R}_{>1} recovers the classical hyperbolic K_3 regulator. The pre-archimedean form respects the Hecke bar-involution; the archimedean form respects the standard \mathbb{R}-valued K-theory.

This refines the discussion in Borromean rings represent a non-trivial element of K_3(\mathbb{C}) / Bloch group with regulator r_2 = 8G: the framework's working object is the pre-archimedean \mathfrak{B}(\widehat{\mathbb{Z}[q]}), and the Beilinson regulator r_2 is the archimedean realization of the graded \rho_K.
